name: 蜃子滩
Shen-Spawn Shallows
before: 荒原尽头一片浅滩，大潮一退，滩上密密麻麻趴满了小蛤，铜钱大，一张一合，每张一回嘴，就吐出一小团光，光里浮着一座指甲大的楼。这是大蜃的蜃子。一伙海盗守在滩上，一筐筐地捡，装进琉璃瓶里卖给城里的阔人当「瓶中楼」，捡不完的就拿脚踩。

A stretch of shallows at the edge of the plain, and when the spring tide goes out it's thick with little clams the size of coins, opening and closing, and each time one opens it breathes out a small ball of light with a fingernail-sized tower floating in it. These are the great shen's spawn. A pirate band holds the shallows, gathering them by the basket to seal in glass jars and sell to rich men in the cities as 'towers in a bottle', and trampling whatever they can't carry.
after: 这一回的海盗被赶下了滩，剩下的蜃子慢慢钻回了泥里，一滩小楼一盏盏熄了。蚌婆说大蜃每逢大潮就放一回蜃子，一年十几回，城里的瓶中楼一时兴，海盗就一茬接一茬地来。「它的孩子，总得有人看着。」过些日子大潮再来，你们还得再来赶一回。

This time the pirates are driven off the shallows, and the remaining spawn slowly burrow back into the mud, their little towers going out one by one. Granny Clam says the great shen releases spawn at every spring tide, a dozen times a year, and while towers in a bottle are the fashion in the cities, the pirates will keep coming, crop after crop. 'Its children need someone watching over them.' When the next spring tide comes, you'll have to come and drive them off again.

name: 壳唇屯
Shell-Lip Hamlet
before: 最东头的蛤户屯就扎在大蜃的壳唇上，屋子沿着一道弯弯的白棱排开，像一串珠子。一伙从钩七手下散出来的海盗不服管，占了屯子，开了蛤户的粮窖，天天喝酒，还拿蛤户的孩子当靶子扔贝壳。地底下的喘气一阵比一阵急，屯里的狗整夜叫个不停。

The easternmost clam-diggers' hamlet sits right on the great shen's shell lip, its houses strung along a curving white ridge like a string of beads. A gang of pirates who broke away from Hook Seven and answer to no one has taken it, opened the diggers' grain pits, drinks all day, and throws shells at the diggers' children for target practice. Beneath the ground the breathing comes faster and faster, and the hamlet's dogs bark all night.
after: 海盗被撵走，屯里的狗不叫了。蛤户们说壳唇这几天合得越来越紧，天上的楼却越来越低，「它在攒最后一口气」。蚌婆把耳朵贴在白棱上，听了很久，抬起头：「它在等人。明天一早，它张嘴。」

The pirates are thrown out and the hamlet's dogs fall silent. The diggers say the shell lip has been closing tighter these last days while the towers in the sky sink lower. 'It's saving up its last breath.' Granny Clam lays her ear to the white ridge and listens a long time, then lifts her head. 'It's waiting for someone. Tomorrow at dawn, it will open.'
first: 粮窖里抄出海盗喝剩的六坛酒、五十袋干蛤、二十石米，还有一筐他们从蛤户家抢来的铜铃，是孩子们挂在脚上、走在壳上不迷路用的。

From the grain pits you seize what the pirates hadn't drunk: six jars of wine, fifty sacks of dried clams, twenty piculs of rice, and a basket of little copper bells taken from the diggers' houses, the ones children tie to their ankles so they don't get lost walking on the shell.
pass: 每次路过，壳唇屯的蛤户都给你们端一碗蛤蜊汤，汤里撒一把粉盐，孩子们摇着脚上的铜铃送你们到屯口：「它今天喘得好，替我们问它好。」

Each time you pass, the Shell-Lip diggers serve you a bowl of clam broth sprinkled with pink salt, and the children see you to the edge of the hamlet jingling the bells on their ankles. 'It's breathing well today. Say hello to it for us.'

name: 乱骑原
Plain of Wild Riders
before: 壳唇外头的荒原上，蜃骑一队接一队地冲，冲的方向却乱了：一队往东，一队往西，两队撞在一起，穿过去，又各自接着冲。有个蛤户老汉牵着牛走过，被一队蜃骑追着砍，牛吓得满原乱跑。几个趁乱打劫的海盗跟在后头，捡蛤户丢下的筐。

On the plain outside the shell lip troop after troop of mirage riders charges, but their directions have gone wrong: one troop east, one west, two collide and pass through each other and charge on. An old clam-digger leading an ox is being chased and hacked at by a troop of riders, and the terrified ox is bolting all over the plain. A few pirates trail along behind, picking up the baskets the diggers drop.
after: 蜃骑散了，海盗跑了，牛也找回来了。蚌婆说它害怕了：这些年往它身上钻眼的人太多，它吐兵出来守着，可记性坏了，认不得谁是谁，见人就当是来钻眼的。「它不是凶，」蚌婆说，「它是糊涂了，又怕。」

The riders scatter, the pirates flee and the ox is found. Granny Clam says it's frightened: too many people have bored holes in it these past years, so it breathes out soldiers to stand guard, but its memory has gone and it can't tell anyone apart, so it takes everyone for a driller. 'It isn't fierce,' she says. 'It's muddled, and afraid.'

name: 壳枢崖
Shell-Hinge Cliff
before: 山脚崖下正是大蜃壳的枢口，两扇壳在这里合拢，缝里透出微微的光。钩七的副手「锥子」不服钩七罢手，带着剩下的采珠海盗和抢来的火药上了崖，又糊里糊涂地被一大队蜃兵围在当中，两边打成一锅粥。钩七站在崖下，冲锥子喊：「停手！米的事，有别的路！」

Under the cliff at the mountain foot lies the great shen's hinge, where the two halves of its shell close together, a faint light seeping from the seam. Hook Seven's deputy Awl won't accept Hook Seven's calling it off and has led the remaining pearl poachers up the cliff with the powder they took, only to be muddle-headedly ringed in by a big troop of mirage soldiers, the two sides tangled in a brawl. Hook Seven stands below the cliff shouting up at Awl: 'Stop! There's another way to get rice!'
after: 锥子一伙败了，火药浇了水。钩七把锥子从崖上扶下来，说山脚的互市要开了，拿干蛤和石料换粮，瘦岛一样能活。蚌婆当场答应：蛤户的晒场，分一半给瘦岛的人。锥子坐在地上哭得像个孩子。崖缝里的光亮了一下，像是松了口气。

Awl's gang is beaten and the powder soaked. Hook Seven helps Awl down from the cliff and tells him the market at the mountain foot is opening; trade dried clams and stone for grain, and Lean Island can live just the same. Granny Clam agrees on the spot: half the diggers' drying yard for the Lean Islanders. Awl sits on the ground and cries like a child. The light in the seam brightens a moment, as if letting out a breath.

name: 蜃母庙
Mirage Mother Temple
before: 山脚一座白石小庙，庙里没有神像，只供着一片门板那么大的旧蛤壳。蜃母教的总坛就在这里，教徒们在山下拦路收「香油」，说蜃母饿了，要拿过路人的货喂她。今天庙前聚了上百个披白麻的教徒，拉着一队蜃兵守门，庙祝站在台阶上念经，越念越急。

A little white stone temple at the mountain foot with no idol inside, only an old clam shell the size of a door on the altar. This is the head temple of the Mirage Mother faith, whose believers block the road below to collect 'incense oil', saying the Mother is hungry and must be fed with travellers' goods. Today a hundred white-robed believers have massed before the temple, with a squad of mirage soldiers at the door, and the temple keeper stands on the steps chanting faster and faster.
after: 蜃兵散了，教徒们跪了一地。老庙祝交出经卷：最早那一页不是经，是一个蛤户十年前亲眼所见，「八月廿八，女船主跪在壳枢前，求蜃母替她记路，记到后来者来」。后来的人照着这一页拜，拜成了教，又成了买卖。庙祝红着脸：「蜃母不吃货。它吃的是记性。」

The mirage soldiers scatter and the believers kneel in rows. The old temple keeper hands over his scriptures: the earliest page isn't scripture at all but something a clam-digger saw with his own eyes ten years ago. 'Twenty-eighth of the eighth month: a woman ship's captain knelt before the hinge and begged the Mirage Mother to remember the road for her, until those who come after arrive.' Later people worshipped by that page until it became a faith, and the faith became a money-making business. The keeper reddens. 'The Mother doesn't eat goods. What she eats is memory.'

name: 磨壳镜坊
Shell-Mirror Workshop
before: 山脚一间镜坊，坊主是个老镜匠，拿大蜃掉下的旧壳磨镜子，磨出来的镜面带一层虹光。去年一伙海盗买走他一车镜子，在盐滩上照假城骗人，他气得封了坊门，发誓不再卖一面。如今那伙海盗又来了，带着蜃弓手堵在坊外，要他再磨十车。

A mirror workshop at the mountain foot whose owner, an old mirror-maker, grinds mirrors from old shell the great shen has shed, their faces glazed with a rainbow sheen. Last year a pirate band bought a cartload of his mirrors and used them to throw up fake cities on the salt flat to trick people, and in his anger he shut up shop and swore never to sell another. Now those pirates are back with mirage archers, blocking his door and demanding ten cartloads more.
after: 海盗被打跑，老镜匠开了坊门，佩服你们，愿意换货，还挑了一面最亮的送给阿汐。他把一面大镜子斜着对准壳唇，让你们看：天亮前那一刻，镜子里映出两扇巨壳缓缓张开，壳里卧着一颗珠子，大得像一座屋，一层裹着一层。「它只在那一刻张嘴。」

The pirates are run off and the old mirror-maker opens his doors and, impressed, is willing to trade, picking out the brightest mirror as a gift for Axi. He angles a big mirror toward the shell lip so you can see: in the moment before dawn, two giant shells slowly part in the glass, and inside lies a pearl as big as a house, layer wrapped in layer. 'That's the only moment it opens.'

name: 问壳洞
Shell-Asking Cave
before: 山脚最深处一个石洞，洞底就是大蜃壳的背，凉凉的，摸上去像一面墙。蚌婆五十年来每有心事就来这里，跟它说话。如今洞口挤满了蜃兵蜃骑，一个个半透明，挤成一团，谁也不让进，连蚌婆也拦：它连守了它五十年的人都认不得了。

A stone cave in the deepest part of the mountain foot, its floor the back of the great shen's shell, cool to the touch and smooth as a wall. For fifty years Granny Clam has come here whenever something weighed on her, to talk to it. Now the cave mouth is jammed with mirage soldiers and riders, all half transparent, crowded together and letting no one in, Granny Clam included: it no longer knows even the woman who has kept it for fifty years.
after: 蜃兵蜃骑散了，蚌婆走到洞底，把脸贴在壳上，像贴着一个老伴的背。她说十年来它把那条路一遍一遍地吐出来，吐得太多，自己的事反倒忘了。「明天一早它张嘴，见了人就打。你们别伤它，打醒它就行。醒了，它会把路交出来，交出来，它就能歇了。」

The mirage soldiers and riders scatter, and Granny Clam goes to the back of the cave and lays her cheek against the shell, as if against the back of an old husband. For ten years, she says, it has breathed out that road again and again, so often that it's forgotten its own things. 'Tomorrow at dawn it opens, and it'll fight whoever it sees. Don't hurt it; just wake it. Once it's awake it'll hand the road over, and once it's handed over, it can rest.'

name: 烟岛分卡
Smoke Island Customs Post
before: 烟岛南岸有一座小小的税卡，门口挂着「蜃楼市舶司烟岛分卡」的牌子，卡里一间簿房、一间仓房、一口温泉池。一伙找千里号宝贝的海盗没找着宝，就占了分卡，在温泉里泡脚，把仓里的米和腌鱼吃得只剩一半，把看卡的老书办关在簿房里，让他替他们记「赢了多少」。

On Smoke Island's south shore stands a tiny customs post, its sign reading 'Mirage Customs House, Smoke Island Post': a ledger room, a storeroom and a hot spring pool. A pirate band that came looking for Qianli treasure and didn't find it has taken over the post instead, soaking their feet in the spring and eating half the rice and salt fish in the store, and they've locked the old clerk in his ledger room to keep a tally of 'how much we've won'.
after: 海盗被赶下了岛，老书办抱着簿子出来，第一件事是给你们登记：「后千里，三百灯，到港。」他翻到前一页，指给你们看，一个月前他就记过一笔：「天上见后千里，三百灯，未到。」「天上先到，地上后到，都得记。」他说总卡在东边，「墨三在等你们对账」。

The pirates are driven off the island and the old clerk comes out hugging his book, and the first thing he does is enter you: 'Houqianli, three hundred lamps, arrived in port.' He turns back a page and shows you an entry made a month ago: 'Houqianli sighted in the sky, three hundred lamps, not yet arrived.' 'Arriving in the sky first and on the ground later, both have to be recorded.' The head house is in the east, he says. 'Mo San is waiting to check accounts with you.'
first: 仓房里抄出海盗吃剩的十袋米、八缸腌鱼、两箱从别处劫来的绸缎，还有一摞海盗记的赢账，老书办看了一眼，说加错了三处。

From the storeroom you seize what the pirates hadn't eaten: ten sacks of rice, eight crocks of salt fish, two chests of silk robbed elsewhere, and a stack of the pirates' tallies of their winnings, which the old clerk glances at and says are wrong in three places.
pass: 每次路过，老书办都让你们在温泉里泡一泡脚，再塞一包温泉水煮的鸡蛋，蛋壳上写着日子：「吃之前看一眼，是哪天煮的，记清楚。」

Each time you pass, the old clerk lets you soak your feet in the hot spring and hands you a packet of eggs boiled in its water, the date written on each shell. 'Look before you eat. Know which day it was boiled.'

name: 蜃楼市舶司
The Mirage Customs House
before: 荒原上一座衙门，一半是砖瓦，一半是光：门楼、照壁是真的，后面那几进院子浮在半空，檐角朝下。衙门口一伙海盗带着蜃兵蜃骑守着，说这里的簿子记着全海的买卖，抢到手，谁家做了什么生意都能拿来敲竹杠。门房里坐着一个瘦书生，埋头写字，外头打成什么样，他都不抬头。

A government compound on the plain, half brick and tile, half light: the gatehouse and spirit wall are real, but the courtyards behind float in mid-air, eaves pointing down. A pirate band with mirage soldiers and riders holds the gate, saying the ledgers here record every trade on the whole sea, and whoever gets hold of them can blackmail anyone for any deal they've ever done. In the gatehouse sits a thin scholar, head down, writing, and whatever happens outside, he never looks up.
after: 海盗被打出了衙门，金银换铁器的买卖重新开了，每天一万。瘦书生这才抬头：墨三，蜃楼市舶司的书办。他把一本簿子推给你们，从泉州港开始，雾海、海上集，你们一路上的每一笔买卖都在上面，一笔不差。「天上照见的，我都记下。」他说十年前沈船主雇了他：「把从这片海过的每一笔买卖记下来，记到会算账的人来对。」他翻到最后一页，空着：「对账的人，还没来。」

The pirates are thrown out of the compound and the trade of metalwork for gold opens again, ten thousand a day. Only now does the thin scholar look up: Mo San, clerk of the Mirage Customs House. He pushes a ledger across to you, and starting from Quanzhou harbour, through the Sea of Fog and the Sea Market, every trade you've made along the way is in it, not one missing. 'Whatever the sky shows, I write down.' Ten years ago Captain Shen hired him, he says: 'Write down every trade that crosses this sea, until someone who can keep accounts comes to check them.' He turns to the last page. It's blank. 'The one to check them hasn't come yet.'

name: 罚没库
Confiscation Store
before: 海岬上一座石库，是市舶司当年存罚没货物的地方，库门上的封条一层压一层。一伙走私的大帮占了石库，最精的人手和一大队蜃兵蜃弓手守在门口：他们在库里翻出了十年前的报关单，要拿去找当年报关的人家要「补税」。墨三一听，袖子一挽就要冲。

A stone storehouse on the headland where the Customs House used to keep confiscated goods, seal pasted over seal on its door. A big smuggling ring has taken it, its best men and a big troop of mirage soldiers and archers guarding the door: inside they've turned up customs declarations from ten years ago and plan to dun the families who filed them for 'back taxes'. Hearing this, Mo San rolls up his sleeves to charge in.
after: 走私帮被打散，报关单一张张收了回来。墨三抽出其中一张：千里号五船的报关单，货、人、船都填得清清楚楚，只有「去处」一栏空着，旁边沈渡批了一行小字：「去处待后来者填。」墨三把单子小心夹进簿子：「她什么都写了，就这一栏，留给别人。」

The smugglers are scattered and the declarations gathered back up one by one. Mo San draws one out: the declaration for the Qianli's five ships, cargo, crew and vessels all filled in clearly, only the 'destination' box left blank, and beside it a line in Shen Du's small hand: 'Destination to be filled in by those who come after.' Mo San slips it carefully into his ledger. 'She wrote everything. This one box she left for someone else.'

name: 晚照楼
Evening Glow Tower
before: 每天傍晚，市舶司后院浮在半空的那座楼上会亮起一盏灯，灯下坐着一个女人，腰挂短刀，低头写字。一伙海盗说那是女鬼，镇不住要出事，排在楼下朝天上放火箭，箭穿过楼，落在荒原上，烧着了一片草。墨三在楼下急得跳脚：「别射！那是东家！」

Every evening a lamp lights in the tower floating above the Customs House's rear courtyard, and beneath it sits a woman with a short blade at her waist, head bent, writing. A pirate band says she's a ghost and there'll be trouble if she isn't laid, and they line up below to shoot fire arrows into the sky; the arrows go through the tower and land on the plain, setting a stretch of grass alight. Below, Mo San is hopping with anguish. 'Don't shoot! That's my employer!'
after: 海盗被赶跑，草火扑灭了。楼上的女人写完一页，抬起头，隔着半空朝你们看了一眼，嘴唇动了动。阿舟读得出她的口形，读了两遍：「账。」灯灭了，楼淡了。墨三说十年来她天天写，可他从没见她抬过头：「她看见你们了。」

The pirates are run off and the grass fire beaten out. The woman in the tower finishes a page, lifts her head and looks across the empty air at you, and her lips move. A Zhou can read her lips; he reads them twice. 'Accounts.' The lamp goes out and the tower fades. In ten years she has written every day, Mo San says, and he's never once seen her look up. 'She saw you.'

name: 包税营
Tax-Farm Camp
before: 沙地上一座营寨，寨门口插着一面「奉市舶司包征」的旗，是一伙包税人：他们说从墨三手里买下了这一路的抽税权，凡是过往的货，十抽三，不交就扣车。其实墨三从没卖过什么。寨里的打手是雇来的刀客，还有一队蜃兵站岗，个个板着脸，像真的衙役。

A stockade on the sand flying a banner reading 'Collecting under contract to the Customs House': a gang of tax farmers who claim they've bought the right to levy duties on this road from Mo San, taking three parts in ten of every load and impounding carts that won't pay. In fact Mo San has never sold anything. Their muscle is hired swordsmen plus a squad of mirage soldiers on sentry duty, all stony-faced like real bailiffs.
after: 包税人被打散，扣下的车都放了。墨三翻开簿子，一笔笔记下他们这几年的勒索，连扣下的一只鸡都记上了。有人问记这些做什么，他说：「账不分好坏，少一笔就对不上。」包税头目捂着脸：「连这个也记？」墨三头也不抬：「尤其是这个。」

The tax farmers are scattered and the impounded carts released. Mo San opens his ledger and enters their extortions of these past years item by item, down to a single confiscated hen. Asked why he bothers, he says, 'Accounts don't sort good from bad. Leave one entry out and they won't balance.' The tax farmers' chief covers his face. 'You're writing that down too?' Mo San doesn't look up. 'That especially.'

name: 三路碑
Three Roads Stele
before: 荒原路口立着一块三面的石碑，一面刻驼，一面刻马，一面刻船。一伙海盗拿它当拴船桩，碑身上缠满了缆绳，还在碑脚下生火烤鱼，烟把碑字熏得漆黑。他们见墨三来擦碑，一脚把他踹开：「一块破石头，擦什么擦！」

At a crossroads on the plain stands a three-sided stele, a camel carved on one face, a horse on another, a ship on the third. A pirate band uses it as a mooring post, its shaft wound with cables, and they roast fish over a fire at its foot until the smoke has blackened the inscriptions. When Mo San comes to clean it they kick him aside. 'It's a lump of old stone. What's there to clean?'
after: 海盗被赶跑，缆绳解了。墨三和阿舟一起擦碑，擦出一行字：「丝、茶、海三路同发，各记一本账。会时合账，账合，路通。千里号立。」墨三擦着擦着停了手：「我这本是海路的。丝路那本，在那位账房先生手里。东家等的，就是他。」

The pirates are chased off and the cables untied. Mo San and A Zhou clean the stele together and uncover a line: 'Silk, Tea and Sea, the three roads set out together, each keeping its own book. When they meet, the books are joined; when the books agree, the road is open. Raised by the Qianli.' Mo San stops scrubbing. 'Mine is the sea road's book. The silk road's is in that bookkeeper's hands. He's the one my employer is waiting for.'

name: 结绳寮
Knot-Cord Hut
before: 市舶司旁边一间草寮，住着墨三的小徒弟小砚，十二岁，不识几个字，记账靠结绳：一根绳一天，大结是大事，小结是小事。一伙海盗听说她的绳子记着「东家几时出来」，要拿去卖给想见鬼的阔人，抢不着就点火烧寮。小砚抱着一大捆绳子爬上了房梁。

Beside the Customs House stands a straw hut where Mo San's little apprentice Xiaoyan lives. She's twelve, knows few characters, and keeps her records in knotted cord: one cord a day, big knots for big things, small knots for small. A pirate band has heard her cords record 'when the employer comes out' and wants them to sell to rich men eager to see a ghost, and failing to grab them they've set the hut alight. Xiaoyan has climbed onto the roof beam clutching a huge bundle of cord.
after: 海盗被赶跑，火扑灭了，绳子一根没烧。小砚把绳子一根根摊在地上：头几年，每根绳上都有个大结，东家天天出来；这两年，十根里只有三根有结；这个月只有一根，就是你们来的那天。「她出来得少了，」小砚说，「可她今天又出来了，是为你们。」

The pirates are run off, the fire put out, not a cord burned. Xiaoyan lays the cords out on the ground one by one. In the early years every cord has a big knot: the employer appeared every day. These past two years only three cords in ten are knotted, and this month only one, the day you arrived. 'She comes out less now,' Xiaoyan says. 'But she came out today. For you.'

name: 隔空楼
Tower Across the Air
before: 这天傍晚，那座楼浮得很低，低得几乎挨着荒原，楼上的女人看得一清二楚：沈渡，短刀，鬓边一缕白发，手边一本账。楼下聚了一伙想发财的海盗，搭了梯子往楼上爬，爬一节，楼就往后退一步，海盗们一齐使劲推梯子，又拉来一队蜃兵帮着扶。

This evening the tower floats very low, almost touching the plain, and the woman on it is plain to see: Shen Du, her short blade, a strand of white at her temple, a ledger at her hand. Below it a pirate band out to get rich has put up ladders to climb in, and with every rung the tower backs away a step, so the pirates all shove the ladders forward together, a squad of mirage soldiers helping hold them steady.
after: 海盗和梯子一起倒了。楼上的沈渡放下笔，隔着半空说话，声音像从很深的水底传上来：「你们来了。账房先生呢？」你们举起丝路带来的那本账。她看了很久，笑了一下：「他向来晚。账要对，得当面对。往东来，到大蜃那儿。」楼淡了，墨三一个字一个字记下。

The pirates topple with their ladders. On the tower Shen Du lays down her brush and speaks across the empty air, her voice far off, as if rising from very deep water: 'You've come. Where's the bookkeeper?' You hold up the ledger you brought from the Silk Road. She looks at it a long time, and smiles a little. 'He's always late. Accounts have to be checked face to face. Come east, to the great shen.' The tower fades, and Mo San writes it all down, word by word.

name: 撕页巷
Torn-Page Lane
before: 市舶司后面一条小巷，巷里开着几家当铺，当的不是东西，是账页：一伙账贼专从市舶司的旧簿子里撕页，谁家的生意上了簿子，就拿那一页上门要钱，不给就把页子贴到城门口。今天账贼又撕了一摞，雇了几个蜃骑守着巷口，等买主上门。

A little lane behind the Customs House lined with pawnshops that take not goods but ledger pages: a gang of ledger thieves tears pages from the Customs House's old books, and whoever's trade appears on a page gets a visit demanding money, or the page goes up on the city gate. Today they've torn out another stack and hired a few mirage riders to guard the lane's mouth while they wait for buyers.
after: 账贼被打跑，撕下的页子全追了回来。墨三一页页对着补，补到一张旧名单，是千里号当年在市舶司登记的船员，六号船那一栏底下，有一行没划掉：「舵手阿舟，未到，留。」阿舟看着那一行，半天才说：「她一直留着。」

The thieves are run off and every torn page recovered. Mo San pastes them back one at a time and comes to an old roster, the crew list the Qianli registered with the Customs House. Under Ship Six is a line that's never been struck through: 'Helmsman A Zhou. Not arrived. Keep.' A Zhou looks at that line a long while before he speaks. 'She kept it all this time.'

name: 寄蜃驿
Post to the Mirage
before: 荒原上一座小驿，是市舶司收信的地方，门口写着「寄蜃楼沈船主，概收」。十年来，沿海各处都有人往这儿寄信。一队发了疯的蜃兵这几天见人就砍，连送信的驿卒也砍，驿卒抱着信袋躲进了马槽，一伙海盗趁机来抢信袋，以为里头是银票。

A small post station on the plain where the Customs House receives mail, a sign at its door: 'Letters for Captain Shen in the Mirage, all accepted.' For ten years people all along the coast have sent letters here. These past days a squad of mirage soldiers gone mad has been hacking at anyone it meets, couriers included, and the courier is hiding in the horse trough clutching his mailbag, while a pirate band seizes the chance to grab the bag, thinking it full of banknotes.
after: 蜃兵散了，海盗跑了，信袋保住了。袋里全是寄给沈渡的信，一封也没拆过：有泉州的，有雾海的，有一封署名「龙四海」，只有一句：「泊位还留着，你们回不回来，都留着。」墨三说东家从不回信，「她说等对完账，一次回」。

The mirage soldiers scatter, the pirates flee, and the mailbag is saved. It's full of letters to Shen Du, not one opened: from Quanzhou, from the Sea of Fog, and one signed 'Long Sihai' with a single line: 'The berth is still kept. Whether you come back or not, it stays kept.' Mo San says his employer never answers letters. 'She says she'll answer them all at once, when the accounts are checked.'

name: 黑账楼
Black Ledger Tower
before: 荒原上一座三层的砖楼，是走私的「黑账帮」的老巢：他们专门伪造账本，替人造假欠条、假契约，这几年造得最多的是「千里号欠条」，拿去找沿海的商户讨十年前的旧债。楼里最凶的打手、蜃兵、蜃弓手层层把守，楼顶上晾着一张张刚做旧的假账页。

A three-storey brick tower on the plain, lair of the smuggling 'Black Ledger Gang': they forge account books, fake IOUs and fake contracts for hire, and these past years their bestseller has been 'Qianli IOUs', used to dun coastal merchants for debts ten years old. Their fiercest bruisers, mirage soldiers and archers guard it floor by floor, and on the roof hang sheets of freshly aged fake ledger pages.
after: 黑账帮被打散，假账页堆在院子里烧了一下午。墨三拿着一张假欠条，和他簿子里千里号的那一页并排一比，摇头：「假的。千里号走的时候，账是平的。」他指着自己簿子上沈渡亲笔的那一行：「千里号，欠：无。」只有最后一行没写完：「欠后来者：」。

The Black Ledger Gang is scattered and their fake pages burn in the yard all afternoon. Mo San lays one fake IOU beside the Qianli's page in his own ledger and shakes his head. 'False. When the Qianli left, its accounts were square.' He points to a line in Shen Du's own hand: 'The Qianli owes: nothing.' Only the very last line is unfinished: 'Owed to those who come after: '.

name: 算盘礁
Abacus Reef
before: 海边一块礁石上坐着个白胡子老头，膝上一把金珠算盘，噼里啪啦打了十年，人称算盘仙。他算的是千里号三路的总账，算一遍，差一文；再算一遍，还差一文。一伙海盗眼红那把金算盘，围着礁石泅水上来抢，老头一边打算盘一边拿脚踹。

On a rock by the sea sits a white-bearded old man with a gold-beaded abacus on his knees, clacking away for ten years now; they call him the Abacus Immortal. He's reckoning the Qianli's grand total across all three roads, and every time he's one copper out; reckon again, still one copper out. A pirate band covets the gold abacus and is swimming out to grab it, and the old man keeps clicking beads with one hand while kicking at them with his feet.
after: 海盗被赶回了海里。算盘仙说那一文不是他算错了，是少了一本：「海路的账在墨三那儿，茶路的有人捎来过一页，丝路的一个字也没有。没有那本，永远差一文。」你们递上丝路账房的账，他翻了几页：「对了，就是这一文。可这得当着东家的面才算数。」

The pirates are driven back into the sea. The Abacus Immortal says the copper isn't his mistake; there's a book missing. 'The sea road's account is with Mo San, someone brought one page of the tea road's, and of the silk road's there's not a word. Without that book I'll always be a copper out.' You hand him the ledger of the Silk Road's bookkeeper. He leafs through a few pages. 'That's it, that's the copper. But it only counts in front of the employer.'

name: 墨家面摊
Mo Family Noodle Stall
before: 市舶司街口一个面摊，摊主是墨三的媳妇墨嫂，面条拉得又细又长。一伙收保护钱的地痞带着几个蜃骑来闹，嫌面摊挡了他们的道，要么交钱，要么搬走。墨嫂一手拿擀面杖，一手拿汤勺：「我男人在衙门里一个月没回家，你们还来添乱！」

A noodle stall at the end of the Customs House's street, kept by Mo San's wife, Mistress Mo, who pulls her noodles long and fine. A gang of protection racketeers has come with a few mirage riders to make trouble: the stall's in their way, so pay up or move. Mistress Mo has a rolling pin in one hand and a ladle in the other. 'My husband hasn't been home from that office in a month, and now you come making trouble too!'
after: 地痞被打跑，墨嫂给你们一人下了一碗面。她说墨三一个月没回家，是因为簿子快满了，就差最后一页，「他说那一页不能他写，得等一个人来，当着东家的面写」。她往面里多卧了个蛋：「你们就是那个人吧？写完了，让他回家吃饭。」

The racketeers are run off and Mistress Mo cooks each of you a bowl of noodles. Mo San hasn't been home in a month, she says, because his ledger is nearly full, all but the last page. 'He says he can't write that page himself. He has to wait for someone to come and write it in front of the employer.' She slips an extra egg into your bowls. 'You're that someone, aren't you? Once it's written, send him home to eat.'

name: 验簿关
Ledger-Check Pass
before: 山脚下一道关口，关楼半真半假，关前站着一排蜃楼里映下来的老关吏，挨个拦人，问的都是同一句：「簿上有你的名字吗？」答不上的，关吏身后的蜃兵就扑上来。关口外头还挤着一伙海盗，想混过关去东边捞好处，被蜃兵砍得东倒西歪。

A pass at the mountain foot, its gate tower half real, half not, and before it a row of old customs officers cast down from the Mirage, stopping everyone in turn with the same question: 'Is your name in the ledger?' Whoever can't answer has the mirage soldiers behind the officers fall on them. A pirate band is crowded outside the pass too, trying to slip through east for pickings and being cut about by the soldiers.
after: 海盗被打散，蜃兵退了。墨三翻开簿子，把你们一路的买卖念给关吏听，念一笔，关吏点一下头，念完，关吏一个个淡了，关门自己开了。墨三说：「做过的买卖，就是过关的凭据。蜃王只认记在簿上的人。」

The pirates are scattered and the mirage soldiers fall back. Mo San opens his ledger and reads out your trades along the road to the officers; with each entry they nod, and when he finishes they fade one by one and the gate opens of its own accord. 'Trades you've made are your pass,' Mo San says. 'The Mirage King only knows people who are written in the ledger.'

name: 买簿庄
Ledger-Buyer's Manor
before: 山脚一座大庄子，庄主是个绰号「金算盘」的大商人，听说墨三的簿子记着全海的买卖，出了一万两要买，买不成就抢：谁家欠谁、谁家偷了税，都在里头，拿到手就能拿捏一海的人。他雇了一大队刀客和蜃弓手，把墨三去东边的路堵得严严实实。

A great manor at the mountain foot whose master, a big merchant nicknamed Golden Abacus, has heard Mo San's ledger records every trade on the sea and offered ten thousand taels for it; refused, he means to take it. Who owes whom, who dodged their duties, it's all in there, and whoever holds it holds the whole sea by the throat. He's hired a big troop of swordsmen and mirage archers and blocked Mo San's road east tight.
after: 刀客被打散，金算盘缩在账房里。墨三翻到他那一页，念了三笔漏税，金算盘的脸一下子白了。墨三合上簿子：「簿子是记路的，不是拿人的。你漏的税，自己去补。」金算盘第二天就去补了，还多交了一成，说是买个安心。

The swordsmen are scattered and Golden Abacus cowers in his counting house. Mo San turns to his page and reads out three dodged duties, and the merchant goes white. Mo San shuts the book. 'This ledger is for recording a road, not for squeezing people. The duties you dodged, go and pay them yourself.' Golden Abacus pays them the very next day, plus an extra tenth, for peace of mind, he says.

name: 三百零一铺
Shop Three Hundred and One
before: 海边一间杂货铺，招牌上写着「千里号伙计开」，铺主是个胖乎乎的中年人，逢人便说他是千里号的人。没人信，一伙海盗更是天天来敲他：「千里号的人？那船上的宝贝藏哪儿了？」不说就砸货架，还拿蜃兵守着铺门，不许人进去买东西，铺子半年没开张。

A general store by the sea, its signboard reading 'Kept by a hand of the Qianli', its owner a plump middle-aged man who tells everyone he's one of the Qianli's people. No one believes him, least of all the pirate band that comes to lean on him every day: 'A Qianli man, eh? Where's that ship's treasure hidden?' When he won't say they smash his shelves, and they've posted mirage soldiers at the door so no one can shop. The store hasn't opened in half a year.
after: 海盗被打跑，阿舟一看见铺主就笑出了声：「你是那个睡过头的！」铺主叫胡十一，十年前最后一天才上名册，第二天开船他睡过了头，追到海边，船已进雾。「第三百零一个，」他挠着头，「船主说我这一行不在名单上，在后头。」他重新开张，换给你们的货件件足秤。

The pirates are run off, and the moment A Zhou sees the owner he bursts out laughing. 'You're the one who overslept!' The owner is Hu Shiyi, signed onto the crew list on the very last day; next morning the ships sailed while he slept on, and by the time he'd chased down to the shore they'd gone into the fog. 'Number three hundred and one,' he says, scratching his head. 'The captain said my line isn't on the list, it comes after.' He opens up again, and every item he trades you is full weight.

name: 抢秤坪
Scramble-for-the-Scale Flat
before: 山脚互市要开张的消息一传出去，各路商贩全涌到了这片坪上，为了谁先上秤吵成一团：瘦岛的人扛着干蛤，蛤户背着贝，盐工赶着盐车，还有一伙海盗冒充商贩，带着蜃骑横冲直撞，要抢头一个位子。墨三被挤在当中，怀里的簿子差点被挤掉。

The moment word goes out that the market at the mountain foot is opening, traders of every kind pour onto this flat and fall to squabbling over who goes on the scale first: Lean Islanders lugging dried clams, clam-diggers with shellfish on their backs, salt workers driving salt carts, and a pirate band posing as traders, charging about with mirage riders to seize the first place. Mo San is jammed in the middle and his ledger nearly gets squeezed out of his arms.
after: 冒充的海盗被打跑，剩下的商贩排起了队，墨三让大家抓阄。抓到头一个的，是瘦岛一个瘦得皮包骨的小姑娘，她扛着一小袋干蛤，往秤盘上一放，眼睛亮亮的。墨三在簿子上记了一笔：「山脚互市，第一笔。」

The fake traders are run off, the rest form a queue, and Mo San has them draw lots. The first lot goes to a little girl from Lean Island, skin and bone, who sets a small sack of dried clams on the scale pan, eyes shining. Mo San writes in his ledger: 'Mountain Foot Market, first trade.'

name: 山脚互市
Mountain Foot Market
before: 山脚下一片平地，正对着大蜃的壳唇，从前是蛤户和山民交换东西的地方，十年前就荒了。如今市口被最后一大伙海盗和蜃兵占着：海盗要独占这条路，蜃兵则什么人都拦，连海盗也拦。墨三把秤和簿子摆在市口的石台上，等你们打开一条路。

A stretch of level ground at the mountain foot facing the great shen's shell lip, once where the clam-diggers and hill folk traded, abandoned ten years ago. Now the market mouth is held by a last big pirate band and mirage soldiers: the pirates want the road to themselves, while the soldiers stop everyone, pirates included. Mo San has set his scale and ledger on a stone table at the market mouth, waiting for you to clear a way.
after: 海盗和蜃兵都散了，粮食换石料的买卖开了张，每天三万。瘦岛的人扛着粮往海边走，钩七走在最后，回头朝蛤户作了个揖。墨三把今天的每一笔都记进簿子，翻到最后一页，还是空着。他把丝路的那本账和自己这本并排摆好：「两本都在，人也到了。」他望着壳唇：「明天一早它张嘴。东家说过，账要当面对。」

The pirates and soldiers scatter and the trade of grain for stone opens for business, thirty thousand a day. The Lean Islanders shoulder their grain toward the shore, Hook Seven walking last, turning back to bow to the clam-diggers. Mo San enters every one of today's trades in his ledger and turns to the last page, still blank. He lays the Silk Road's book beside his own. 'Both books are here, and so are the people.' He looks toward the shell lip. 'Tomorrow at dawn it opens. The employer said accounts have to be checked face to face.'

name: 封港湾
Blockaded Bay
before: 市舶司的小港被一大片海盗船堵住了，船上的人说是「来对账的」：他们听说市舶司要把全海的账对一遍，怕自家的旧账翻出来，干脆把港口封了，一条船也不许进出。船头站着蜃弓手，船舷挂着蜃兵，远看像一支水师，近了才看出一半是影子。

The Customs House's little harbour is choked by a great crowd of pirate ships whose crews say they've 'come to check accounts': hearing the Customs House means to reconcile every account on the sea, and afraid their own old debts will come to light, they've simply blockaded the port, letting no ship in or out. Mirage archers stand in the bows and mirage soldiers hang along the rails, so from afar it looks like a navy, and only up close can you see half of it is shadow.
after: 海盗船队被打散，港口通了。被俘的海盗头子垂头丧气：「我们那些旧账，是不是都在簿子上？」墨三说在，一笔不少。海盗头子叹了口气：「那就记着吧，往后的，记好看点。」港里的船又能进出了，有一条装着粮，往瘦岛去。

The pirate fleet is broken and the harbour opens. The captured pirate chief hangs his head. 'Those old accounts of ours, are they all in the book?' Mo San says they are, every one. The chief sighs. 'Then keep them. Make what comes after look better.' Ships can come and go again, and one of them, loaded with grain, is bound for Lean Island.

name: 封账阁
Sealed Account Pavilion
before: 海边崖上一座小阁，阁门贴着市舶司的封条，封条上是沈渡的印。墨三十年没敢开过：东家吩咐，后来者来了才开。一伙海盗认定阁里是千里号的藏宝图，带着最精的手下和一大队蜃兵蜃骑守在崖上，正拿斧子劈门，墨三扑上去，被一脚踹到崖边。

A small pavilion on a seaside cliff, its door pasted with a Customs House seal bearing Shen Du's stamp. Mo San hasn't dared open it in ten years: his employer said it was to be opened only when those who come after arrived. A pirate band is sure it holds the Qianli's treasure map, and with their best men and a big troop of mirage soldiers and riders they hold the cliff and are hacking at the door with axes. Mo San throws himself at them and is kicked to the cliff edge.
after: 海盗被打下崖。墨三揭了封条，阁里只有一本小账，是沈渡自己的：「欠鲍老针工钱一半，回程付。欠戚守光灯油十斤，已由其孙女还。欠旱海军一月饷，已存烟岛。欠复日城一个明天。欠后来者：一条路。」墨三叹气：「别的都还上了，就这一笔，她自己还不了。」

The pirates are driven off the cliff. Mo San peels off the seal. Inside there's only a small account book: Shen Du's own. 'Owed to Bao Laozhen: half his wages, payable on return. Owed to Qi Shouguang: ten jin of lamp oil, repaid by his granddaughter. Owed to the Dry Sea Army: one month's pay, stored on Smoke Island. Owed to Same-Day Town: one tomorrow. Owed to those who come after: a road.' Mo San sighs. 'Everything else is paid. This one she can't pay by herself.'

name: 壳前道
Road Before the Shell
before: 通往壳唇的最后一段路，两边是低矮的山石，路面平得反常，踩上去微微发软。一伙走投无路的海盗守在这里，后头是蜃兵，前头是你们，他们进退两难，干脆横下一条心，在路上挖了陷坑，摆好了阵。地底下的喘气，一下比一下重。

The last stretch of road to the shell lip, low rocks on either side, the surface unnaturally flat and slightly soft underfoot. A band of pirates with nowhere left to go holds it, mirage soldiers behind them and you in front, trapped both ways, so they've steeled themselves, dug pit traps in the road and drawn up for battle. Beneath the ground the breathing comes heavier with every breath.
after: 海盗败了，扔了刀坐在路边。他们说这几天夜里，天上的楼一晚比一晚低，前天楼脚挨着了海面，昨天楼里的人一个个往东走，走进壳唇里就不见了。「像是在收摊，」一个海盗说，「它要把吐出去的东西都收回去。」

The pirates are beaten, throw down their blades and sit by the road. These past nights, they say, the towers in the sky have sunk lower each night; two days ago their feet touched the sea, and yesterday the people in them walked east one by one and vanished into the shell lip. 'Like packing up a stall,' one says. 'It's taking back everything it's breathed out.'

name: 海苔纸寮
Seaweed Paper Hut
before: 海边一间纸寮，寮主是个老纸匠，拿海苔和破网捣浆造纸，纸带着一股海腥味，可结实，泡了水也不烂，市舶司的簿子全用他的纸。一伙海盗占了纸寮，把造好的纸拿去糊船缝，纸浆缸里泡上了他们的臭袜子，老纸匠被赶到寮外，蹲在礁石上抹眼泪。

A papermaking hut by the sea whose owner, an old papermaker, pounds seaweed and worn-out nets into pulp. His paper smells of the sea but it's tough and won't fall apart even soaked, and every ledger at the Customs House is made of it. A pirate band has taken the hut, using the finished paper to caulk their hulls and steeping their reeking socks in the pulp vats, and the old man, driven outside, squats on the rocks wiping his eyes.
after: 海盗被赶跑，纸浆缸换了清水。老纸匠说十年前沈船主在他这儿订过一刀纸，说是给最后一页用的，「要最结实的，一百年不烂」。那刀纸一直没人来取。他把纸包好递给墨三：「最后一页，用这个写。」

The pirates are chased off and the pulp vats refilled with clean water. Ten years ago, the old papermaker says, Captain Shen ordered a quire of paper from him for 'the last page'. 'The toughest you've got. A hundred years without rotting.' No one has ever come to collect it. He wraps it and hands it to Mo San. 'Write the last page on this.'
first: 纸寮里抄出海盗囤的四十捆干海苔、六袋米、一桶鱼油，还有他们抢来糊船的三百张好纸，老纸匠一张张抚平，说还能用。

From the hut you seize the pirates' stores: forty bundles of dried seaweed, six sacks of rice, a cask of fish oil, and three hundred sheets of good paper they'd grabbed to caulk their boats, which the old papermaker smooths flat one by one, saying they'll still serve.
pass: 每次路过，老纸匠都给你们一叠海苔纸和一包烤海苔，说：「纸记事，海苔管饱。路上的事记下来，别全指望脑子。」

Each time you pass, the old papermaker gives you a sheaf of seaweed paper and a packet of toasted seaweed. 'Paper for remembering, seaweed for filling up. Write down what happens on the road. Don't leave it all to your head.'

name: 对账台
Reckoning Terrace
before: 壳唇前一块平平的白石，像一张大案。墨三把两本账摆上去，海路一本，丝路一本，铺开那刀海苔纸。天快亮了，壳唇边浮起一层光，光里走出一个人：沈渡，短刀，白发，手里也拿着一本账。她把账放在案的另一头，看着你们：「账房先生呢？」你们替他说：「他晚到了。」话音没落，案边的地里一排排站起了蜃兵，围住了石案。

Before the shell lip lies a flat white stone like a great desk. Mo San sets out two books on it, the sea road's and the silk road's, and spreads out the quire of seaweed paper. Dawn is near; a sheen of light rises along the shell lip, and out of it walks a figure: Shen Du, short blade, white hair, a ledger in her hand too. She lays it at the far end of the desk and looks at you. 'Where's the bookkeeper?' You answer for him: 'He's late.' Before the words are out, rank upon rank of mirage soldiers rise from the ground around the desk and close in on the stone.
after: 蜃兵散了，沈渡没有动。她翻开丝路的账，看到「丝路，对毕」，眼睛红了：「他还是那么爱算。」三本账并排摆着，只差一样：「大蜃替我记着的那条路。它记了十年，快记不住了，我要你们把它写下来。」她指着壳唇：「天一亮它张嘴。它谁也不认得了，得先打醒它。」

The mirage soldiers scatter. Shen Du hasn't moved. She opens the silk road's book, sees the last words, 'Silk Road: accounts settled', and her eyes redden a moment. 'Still so fond of his sums.' Three books lie side by side, and one thing is missing. 'The road the great shen has been remembering for me. Ten years it's kept it, and it can hardly hold it any more. I need you to write it down.' She points at the shell lip. 'At first light it opens. It doesn't know anyone now. You'll have to wake it first.'

name: 蜃王
The Mirage King
before: 天亮了。脚下的荒原整个一动，壳唇裂开，两扇白壳缓缓张起，大得望不到头，你们才知道自己一直站在它背上。壳里的光一层层涌出来，蜃楼一齐落到地上：海市、复日城、旱海军的阵、千里号的五条船、一条灯路。接着是兵，蜃兵、蜃弓手、蜃骑三路排开，它谁也不认得，只认得要守住那条路。你们把一路的东西摆在壳前：真假簿、老秤的账、军主令、蚌婆送回的珠子、墨三的簿子。

Day breaks. The whole plain shifts underfoot, the shell lip parts, and two white shells slowly rise, so vast you can't see their ends, and only now do you realise you've been standing on its back all along. Light pours from the shell layer upon layer and the whole Mirage comes down to earth at once: the Sea Market, Same-Day Town, the Dry Sea Army's ranks, the Qianli's five ships, a road of lamps. Then come the soldiers, mirage infantry, archers and riders drawn up in three wings; it knows no one now, only that the road must be guarded. You lay out before the shell everything from the way: the Real-or-Not Book, Old Scale's ledger, the Commander's Token, the pearls Granny Clam returned, Mo San's book.
after: 兵散了，壳里传出一支歌，很慢，很低，是阿汐她爹哄她睡觉的那支，唱到最后一句：「阿汐。」阿汐跪在壳前，跟着唱完。灯路最后亮了一回，一盏不缺，从西往东，墨三一盏一盏写上海苔纸，阿舟每念一盏，就在卤妹的真假簿上记一个「真」。路的尽头，海是静的。沈渡合上账：「账对上了。三路的人都往那儿去了，归墟见。」她走进灯路，越走越远。两扇壳慢慢合上，地下的喘气终于匀了：它不用再记了。

The soldiers scatter, and from the shell comes a song, very slow and very low, the one Axi's father used to sing her to sleep, and at the last line: 'Axi.' Axi kneels before the shell and sings it through with it. The road of lamps shines one last time, every lamp there, west to east, and Mo San writes them onto the seaweed paper one by one, and for each lamp A Zhou reads out, he marks 'Real' in Lumei's Real-or-Not Book. At the road's end, the sea lies still. Shen Du closes her ledger. 'The accounts agree. The people of all three roads have gone that way. I'll see you at the Return Ruins.' She walks into the road of lamps and goes farther and farther away. The two shells slowly close, and the breathing under the ground is even at last: it doesn't have to remember any more.
